title: Remove and unplug Limit/Home sensor (A-axis or Z-axis)
summary: LOTO the tipper, unplug and remove a defective Limit/Home proximity sensor (A-axis or Z-axis), and route the sensor cable through the wire routing hole for replacement.
when_to_use: Use when a Limit/Home proximity sensor is defective and must be removed (A-axis sensor or Z-axis sensor) so it can be replaced, including preparing the cable routing for the new sensor.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: perform LOTO and physical sensor removal/unplugging and cable routing preparation.
safety_notes: Perform LOTO of the tipper before unplugging/removing the sensor.
access_or_tools_needed: Replacement part: Limit sensor or home sensor
Access to tipper for LOTO and to sensor connection points (PCA near A-axis motor or CLINK controller inside control box)

external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout (referenced on page 2 in the manual section).

visual_references.description: A-Axis PCA connections showing A-axis wire routing through the wire routing hole and fastening with an M3 button-head screw; also shows where A-axis sensor wires plug into the PCA.
Z-Axis CLINK connections showing Z-axis wires dropping through the column and out the lower grommet into the control box and plugging into I/O1, DI6, or DI7.
Flat-Flex Cable (FFC) diagram at the A-axis PCA showing the M3 socket-head screws and FFC clamps (useful for understanding the A-axis PCA connection area).
CLINK controller diagram showing the controller box and cable connections (useful for understanding the Z-axis sensor connection point inside the control box).

steps.title: Identify whether the defective sensor is A-axis or Z-axis
steps.purpose: Ensure you unplug the sensor from the correct connection point (PCA near A-axis motor vs CLINK controller inside control box).
steps.instruction: Use the sensor location guidance to determine whether the defective Limit/Home sensor is an A-axis sensor or a Z-axis sensor.
steps.expected_result: You can classify the sensor as either A-axis or Z-axis based on its location/connection point.
steps.healthy_condition: A-axis sensor is identified as being plugged into a printed circuit assembly (PCA) near the A-axis motor; Z-axis sensor is identified as being plugged into the CLINK controller inside the control box.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot determine whether the sensor is A-axis or Z-axis, or you identify the wrong connection point type.

actions.label: Classify sensor location
actions.exact_action: Review sensor locations on the previous page ("Sensors" section) to identify whether the sensor is A-axis or Z-axis.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the sensor connection point cannot be identified (PCA near A-axis motor vs CLINK controller inside control box), stop and re-check sensor location guidance.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: NOTE: See "Sensors" on the previous page for sensor locations. A-axis sensors are plugged into a PCA near the A-axis motor; Z-axis sensors are plugged into the CLINK controller inside the control box.

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.purpose: Make the tipper safe for unplugging/removal work.
steps.instruction: LOTO the tipper using the manual’s Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out/tagged out prior to unplugging the sensor.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is applied before any sensor unplugging/removal actions.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to unplug/remove the sensor without LOTO.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 1. LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Unplug the sensor
steps.purpose: Disconnect the sensor electrically so it can be removed from its mounting location.
steps.instruction: Unplug the sensor from its connection point.
steps.expected_result: The sensor is unplugged from its connection point (PCA near A-axis motor for A-axis; CLINK controller inside control box for Z-axis).
steps.healthy_condition: Unplugging is performed at the correct connection point for the identified sensor type.
steps.failure_condition: You unplug from an incorrect location or cannot access/unplug the sensor due to misidentification.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the sensor connection point cannot be identified (PCA near A-axis motor vs CLINK controller inside control box), stop and re-check sensor location guidance.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 2. Unplug the sensor. A-axis sensors are plugged into a printed circuit assembly (PCA) near the A-axis motor. Z-axis sensors are plugged into the CLINK controller inside the control box.

steps.title: Remove the sensor mounting screw and feed the sensor through the wire routing hole
steps.purpose: Release the sensor from its mounting location and free the cable for removal.
steps.instruction: Remove the M3 button-head screw holding the sensor in place, then feed the sensor through the hole where the wire is routed.
steps.expected_result: The M3 button-head screw is removed and the sensor is fed through the wire routing hole.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor is loosened and can be pulled away from the column area (A-axis) or pulled from the column (Z-axis) after feeding through the wire routing hole.
steps.failure_condition: Sensor remains secured because the M3 screw was not removed or the sensor cannot be fed through the wire routing hole.

actions.label: Remove M3 screw and feed sensor
actions.exact_action: Remove the M3 button-head screw holding the sensor in place and feed it through the hole in which the wire is routed.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 3. Remove the M3 button-head screw holding the sensor in place and feed it through the hole in which the wire is routed.

steps.title: Pull the sensor out (A-axis vs Z-axis handling)
steps.purpose: Complete physical removal of the defective sensor from its mounting location.
steps.instruction: If removing an A-axis sensor, pull the sensor away from the column area; if removing a Z-axis sensor, pull the sensor from the column. If the A-axis sensor is defective, cut the wire tie if needed.
steps.expected_result: The defective sensor is removed from its mounting location: A-axis sensor pulled away from the column area; Z-axis sensor pulled from the column.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor is free and removed without damaging the cable routing; any required wire tie is cut to allow removal.
steps.failure_condition: Sensor does not pull free (wire tie may need to be cut) or removal damages cable routing.

actions.label: Pull A-axis sensor
actions.exact_action: A defective A-axis sensor is pulled away, but the wire tie may need to be cut.

actions.label: Pull Z-axis sensor
actions.exact_action: Pull the Z-axis sensor from the column.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the sensor does not pull free, cut the wire tie (noted as potentially required for a defective A-axis sensor).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 4. Pull the Z-axis sensor from the column. A defective A-axis sensor is pulled away, but the wire tie may need to be cut.

steps.title: Optional: use the new sensor to pull through cable routing
steps.purpose: Make cable routing for the replacement easier by using the new sensor to pull the cable through the routing path.
steps.instruction: If beneficial, connect the new sensor to the one being replaced to pull through the cable routing so it is routed properly and easier.
steps.expected_result: Cable routing is prepared so the replacement sensor can be routed properly through the wire routing path.
steps.healthy_condition: Replacement sensor cable can be routed through the hole/wire routing path without excessive resistance.
steps.failure_condition: Cable routing is not properly guided through the routing hole/path, increasing risk of pinching or incorrect routing.

actions.label: Connect sensors for pull-through
actions.exact_action: it may be beneficial to connect the new sensor to the one being replaced to pull through the cable routing so it is routed properly and easier.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: NOTE: it may be beneficial to connect the new sensor to the one being replaced to pull through the cable routing so it is routed properly and easier.

success_criteria: Defective Limit/Home sensor is unplugged and removed from its mounting location (A-axis sensor pulled away from column area; Z-axis sensor pulled from the column).
Sensor cable is routed through the hole where the wire is routed, with any wire tie cut as needed.
healthy_conditions: A-axis sensor removal: sensor pulled away from the column area; wire tie cut only if needed for a defective A-axis sensor.
Z-axis sensor removal: sensor pulled from the column.
failure_conditions: Sensor does not pull free and wire tie was not cut when needed (A-axis defective sensor case).
Sensor connection point cannot be identified (PCA near A-axis motor vs CLINK controller inside control box).
escalation_guidance: If you cannot identify whether the sensor is A-axis or Z-axis, stop and re-check the sensor location guidance referenced by the manual’s Sensors page.
If the sensor cannot be removed after cutting the wire tie (when applicable), stop and escalate to maintenance/engineering support for further inspection of the mounting and routing.
